facts.text: Summerlin takes its name from Howard Hughes’ paternal grandmother, Jean Amelia Summerlin, whose family owned the land before the 1970s.
Howard Hughes bought 30,000 acres in 1952 for just $3 an acre, sparking the first large‑scale master‑planned community in Nevada.
In 1994 the Summa Corporation rebranded as the Howard Hughes Corporation, keeping the original land holdings and continuing Summerlin’s growth.
A 1990 deal traded 5,000 acres of sensitive land for 3,000 more suitable for building, easing environmental concerns before construction began.
Downtown Summerlin opened in 2014 as a 106‑acre hub of shops, restaurants and entertainment, marking a major shift from residential to mixed‑use development.
Summerlin sits in the Mojave Desert, where summer highs routinely exceed 100 °F and temperatures as high as 118 °F have been recorded.
